Conditionals Maze

Many coding lessons begin with syntax, but I wanted learners to focus on problem-solving first. Players guide a character through a maze by choosing commands, testing sequences, and debugging logic with immediate visual feedback. The game builds intuition for Boolean logic, conditionals, and program flow before learners ever touch formal programming syntax.

What it demonstrates: interactive CS concept design, puzzle-based learning, rapid AI-assisted prototyping, and learner feedback loops.

Featured

Day 1: Intro to Data Science, Research, and the R Language

This is Day 1 of the Data Science Research Program, the first notebook students open. It frames what data science is, how it connects to research, and then immediately puts learners into R: objects, vectors, modes, conditionals, loops, and sequences. The activity at the end has students make a vector from the letters of their name. It's low stakes, personal, and immediately useful. The notebook is designed to be taught live, moving from concept to worked example to student practice throughout. Developed as Day 1 of a 5-week national program I directed for 150+ high school students, many with no prior programming background.

What it demonstrates: first-day scaffolding for absolute beginners, R fundamentals in a research context, and the program's teach → do together → try on your own structure.

Science Is for Everyone

A 2.5-minute science advocacy video tracing the path from a curious child to a working scientist, then asking what happens when that path disappears. Written, narrated, and edited as a public science communication piece during the 2025 federal science funding cuts. 10k views on Instagram.

A hands-on demo using yarn, color, and audience participation to turn 3D genome organization into a physical model learners could inspect, count, and translate into a data visualization. Presented at my PhD defense to ~150 attendees.

Blood Flow Lesson Plans

A full-body kinesthetic lesson where students become blood droplets traveling through parts of the circulatory system (atria, ventricles, arteries, and veins) by moving along a string-marked pathway to a choreographed song. Taught in Kenya and adapted for a California elementary classroom.
